subject: Post-call synthesis & POC sprint playbook — Atlas Bio
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@atlasbio.ai>, Sara Malik <sara.malik@atlasbio.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call synthesis & POC sprint playbook — Atlas Bio

Hi Oliver / Sara —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Short note to capture what we heard and the proposed POC/POC sprint that will let Atlas Bio validate latency, extraction accuracy, and cost at scale. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you emphasized
- High false-positive entity extraction from instrument logs (esp. readouts with OCR noise)
- Latency variability for batch reports impacting downstream QA pipelines
- Cost leakage from repeated prompt invocations on archived records

Goals for a 4-week POC
1) Precision target: reduce false-positive entity extraction from 24% -> <=10% on sampled OCR logs
2) Latency target: 95th pctile generation / extraction < 300ms for single-record lookups (50 tokens)
3) Cost target: demonstrate >=35% per-record unit cost reduction vs current baseline using batching + prefix caching

Scope & success metrics (deliverables)
- Evaluation suite: 1k labeled OCR log samples (we'll provide a seed set, you provide augmentations)
- Prompt set & eval harness: we attach an initial prompt set (poc_prompt-set-v1.jsonl) and will iterate with you
- Throughput test: steady-state 100 qps for 10 minutes to validate autoscaling and 95th pctile latency
- E2E demo: integrated inference into one QA job in your staging environment

Owners and roles
- Atlas Bio: Oliver (POC lead) — test data, access to staging; Sara — QA acceptance criteria & sampling
- Redwood: Kimberly (eng engagement lead) — program coordination; Marcus (runtime lead) — perf & infra; Priyom (evals) — prompt/eval authoring and metrics dashboard

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): access & onboarding, sign off on scope doc
- Week 1: prompt tuning + seed eval run (we iterate twice)
- Week 2: load/throughput validation and autoscaling tests
- Week 3: E2E integration with your QA job; final acceptance run
- Week 4: wrap, handoff, and recommendations report

Access / setup asks we need from Atlas Bio (attached checklist)
- Staging service account + temporary API key (or whitelist IPs)
- Sample OCR corpus (S3/Drive link) + schema for logs
- A staging endpoint for the QA job or short-term SSH access to the runner

Attachments: atlas_poc_scope.pdf (scope doc), access_checklist.xlsx (access & creds), poc_prompt-set-v1.jsonl (seed prompts)

Next steps (immediate)
1) Oliver: confirm the staging access approach by EOD Thursday
2) Redwood: we'll post the shared Drive folder and HubSpot M.A.P. (HS-345672)
3) Schedule kickoff engineering call — propose Mon Aug 2, 9am PT

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Subject: Re: Post-call synthesis & POC sprint playbook — Atlas Bio

Kimberly — thanks for the clear write-up. This aligns with our internal read. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data access: we can share the OCR corpus via an S3 presigned URL (will send by EOD Thu). Does Redwood prefer a particular object layout?
2) Security: we will need a short security questionnaire filled for the staging service account. Can Marcus own that with our security team?
3) Latency expectation: the 300ms 95th pctile is aggressive — can you document the test harness you plan to run so we can validate comparably on our side?

Also Sara asked whether the POC will write any persistent data back to our staging cluster. If so we need to table that until Week 3.

Assuming those answers look good, August 2 kickoff is fine. I'll get internal stakeholders calendar invites out.

Thanks,
Oliver

Oliver — happy to own the security questionnaire with your team. We'll also publish the exact harness and artifacts we run for latency/throughput so you can reproduce locally. Highlights: 

- Harness: JMeter + a lightweight runner that calls Redwood's staging endpoint. We'll publish the runner + configs to the shared Drive folder (link below).
- Workload shape: 50-token median, 95-token tail; burst window simulation + steady-state 100 qps for 10 minutes for autoscaling validation.
- Data handling: we will not write back into your staging cluster during Weeks 0–2. Week 3 E2E integration can use a sandboxed write path; we'll demo and hand off to your infra team before any persistent writes.

I also attached a small checklist of expected IAM roles and a recommended minimal policy for the temporary service account. If you can provide a presigned S3 URL, we will pull the seed corpus into a sandboxed bucket and scrub anything that looks like PII before evals.

I'll drop the harness + configs in Drive by EOD Mon. If you want, Priyom can lead a short walkthrough on Wed to align on evaluation labeling.

Best,
